about: Chapter 12, Racing Seconds: 68 patterns, three or four for each of the 15 skills (1 and 2 marks), three 3-mark and three 5-mark written questions, and three 4-mark case studies, drawn from the chapter's 500 questions. Clock times are HH:MM (24-hour) unless a.m. or p.m. is written; a clock-time answer is two boxes, hours and minutes. All DRAFT until Ashalatha approves them.

choice.e: a walk round the school ground
a train journey from Delhi to Agra
a long bus ride to another city
a green mango ripening on a shelf

patterns.text: Which unit is most suitable for timing {t.e}?

wrong.mistake: chooses a unit by habit rather than by how long the event lasts
chooses a unit by habit rather than by how long the event lasts
chooses a unit by habit rather than by how long the event lasts

patterns.hint: Think how long it really lasts: a moment, a few minutes, part of a day, or many days?
patterns.explanation: The time for {t.e} is best measured in {t.c}s.
patterns.misconception: Selects a unit by the size of the number rather than the length of the event.
patterns.notes: 24 events, six for each of second, minute, hour and day, so the right unit changes; the wrong options are the other three units.

choice.e: running 100 m in a school race
a train journey from Delhi to Mumbai
a flight from Delhi to Chennai
a day trip to a nearby fort

patterns.text: Which is the most sensible time for {t.e}?

wrong.mistake: looks only at the number and not at the unit
looks only at the number and not at the unit
looks only at the number and not at the unit

patterns.hint: All the choices have the same number. Which unit makes it sensible?
patterns.explanation: {t.e} takes {t.c}.
patterns.misconception: Selects a unit by the size of the number rather than the length of the event.
patterns.notes: 16 events; every option has the same number, only the unit changes, and the right unit changes from copy to copy.

patterns.text: A {n}-second {act} is done {k} times without a break. Find the total time in seconds.
patterns.hint: Multiply the time for one by the number of times.
patterns.explanation: {k} × {n} seconds = {n * k} seconds.
patterns.misconception: Selects a unit by the size of the number rather than the length of the event.
patterns.notes: 5 to 30 seconds, done 2 to 6 times.

patterns.responseFormat: Clock time in two boxes (hours; minutes)
patterns.text: On a clock, the minute hand points to {t.k} and the hour hand is {t.pos}. What time does the clock show? Enter hours; minutes.
patterns.hint: The hour is the number the hour hand has passed. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the minute hand.
patterns.explanation: The hour hand has passed {t.h}, so the hour is {t.h}. The minute hand on {t.k} means {t.k} × 5 = {5 * t.k} minutes. The time is {t.h}:{'0' if (5 * t.k) < 10 else ''}{5 * t.k}.
patterns.misconception: Interchanges the hour and minute hands or reads the minute-hand number as minutes rather than groups of five.
patterns.notes: Hours 1 to 11, minute hand on 1 to 11 (5 to 55 minutes); the hour hand is described where it really is (just past, halfway, or nearer the next number); two boxes.

patterns.text: How many five-minute jumps does the minute hand make to move from {a} to {b}?
patterns.hint: Count the numbers the minute hand passes: each one is a five-minute jump.
patterns.explanation: From {a} to {b} is {b - a} {'number' if (b - a) == 1 else 'numbers'}, so {b - a} five-minute jumps ({5 * (b - a)} minutes).
patterns.misconception: Interchanges the hour and minute hands or reads the minute-hand number as minutes rather than groups of five.
patterns.notes: From one clock number to a later one, without passing 12.

patterns.text: On a clock, the minute hand points to {t.k} and the hour hand is {t.pos}. Which time is shown?

wrong.mistake: reads the number the minute hand points to as the minutes
swaps the hour hand and the minute hand
takes the number the hour hand is nearest, or has not reached, as the hour

patterns.hint: The hour is the number the short hand has passed. The long hand counts in fives.
patterns.explanation: Hour {t.h}; the minute hand on {t.k} means {t.k} × 5 minutes, so the time is {t.c}.
patterns.misconception: Interchanges the hour and minute hands or reads the minute-hand number as minutes rather than groups of five.
patterns.notes: Hours 2 to 10, minute hand on 2 to 11 (never on the hour's own number or the next one, so the choices differ); the hour hand is described where it really is.

patterns.text: At the start of a game the minute hand points to {a}. When the game ends, less than an hour later, it points to {b}. How many minutes did the game last? Show your working.

steps.text: Counts the numbers passed going clockwise from {a} to {b}: {(b - a) % 12}.
Multiplies by 5: {5 * ((b - a) % 12)} minutes.

patterns.hint: Go clockwise from {a}. If you pass 12, keep counting.
patterns.explanation: Clockwise from {a} to {b} is {(b - a) % 12} numbers, and each is 5 minutes: {5 * ((b - a) % 12)} minutes.
patterns.misconception: Interchanges the hour and minute hands or reads the minute-hand number as minutes rather than groups of five.
patterns.notes: Minute-hand positions 1 to 11; often the hand passes 12, so the child cannot just subtract.

patterns.text: A runner starts when the seconds hand points to {a} and stops when it points to {b}, less than a minute later. How long did the run take, in seconds?
patterns.hint: Each number on the clock is 5 seconds for the seconds hand. Go clockwise.
patterns.explanation: Clockwise from {a} to {b} is {(b - a) % 12} {'number' if ((b - a) % 12) == 1 else 'numbers'}: {(b - a) % 12} × 5 = {5 * ((b - a) % 12)} seconds.
patterns.misconception: Treats one clock number as one second or assumes a minute contains 100 seconds.
patterns.notes: Any two different positions 1 to 12; the hand may pass 12.

patterns.text: How many seconds are there in {f.a}/{f.b} of a minute?
patterns.hint: A minute has 60 seconds. Find {f.a}/{f.b} of 60.
patterns.misconception: Treats one clock number as one second or assumes a minute contains 100 seconds.
patterns.notes: 26 fractions in halves, thirds, quarters, fifths, sixths, tenths and twelfths (some not in lowest terms, such as 2/4), so the answer is always a whole number of seconds.

patterns.text: The seconds hand points to {a}. Which number will it point to {s} seconds later?
patterns.hint: Every 5 seconds the hand moves on one number. After 12 comes 1.
patterns.explanation: {s} seconds is {s // 5} {'number' if (s // 5) == 1 else 'numbers'} on. From {a}, that is {(a + s // 5 - 1) % 12 + 1}.
patterns.misconception: Treats one clock number as one second or assumes a minute contains 100 seconds.
patterns.notes: Start 1 to 12, 5 to 55 seconds later; the hand often passes 12.

patterns.text: A stopwatch's seconds hand starts at 12, goes round {n} full {'time' if n == 1 else 'times'} and then moves on from 12 to {k}. How many seconds have passed? Show your working.

steps.text: Full turns: {n} × 60 = {60 * n} seconds; then {k} × 5 = {5 * k} seconds.
Adds: {60 * n + 5 * k} seconds.

patterns.hint: One full turn of the seconds hand is 60 seconds.
patterns.misconception: Treats one clock number as one second or assumes a minute contains 100 seconds.
patterns.notes: 1 to 4 full turns, then 5 to 55 seconds more.

patterns.text: Convert {m} minutes to seconds.
patterns.hint: 1 minute = 60 seconds.
patterns.explanation: {m} × 60 = {60 * m} seconds.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 seconds per minute or records a remainder of 60 seconds.
patterns.notes: 2 to 30 minutes.

patterns.text: Write {t} seconds in minutes and seconds. Enter minutes; seconds.
patterns.hint: Take out as many 60s as you can. What is left is the seconds.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 seconds per minute or records a remainder of 60 seconds.
patterns.notes: 65 to 595 seconds, never a whole number of minutes; two boxes.

patterns.text: How many seconds longer is {a} minutes than {b} {'minute' if b == 1 else 'minutes'} {c} seconds?
patterns.hint: Change both to seconds, or think how many seconds make the next full minute.
patterns.explanation: {a} min = {60 * a} sec and {b} min {c} sec = {60 * b + c} sec. {60 * a} − {60 * b + c} = {60 * a - 60 * b - c} seconds.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 seconds per minute or records a remainder of 60 seconds.
patterns.notes: 3 to 9 whole minutes against a shorter time of 1 to 8 minutes and 5 to 55 seconds.

patterns.text: Which is the correct way to write {x.t} seconds in minutes and seconds?

wrong.mistake: leaves 60 or more seconds in the seconds part
uses 100 seconds for a minute
counts one minute too many

patterns.hint: Take out as many 60s as you can; the seconds part must be less than 60.
patterns.explanation: {x.t} seconds = {x.c}.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 seconds per minute or records a remainder of 60 seconds.
patterns.notes: 2 to 8 minutes and 10 to 55 seconds; the wrong choices keep 60 or more seconds, use 100 seconds per minute, or add a minute.

patterns.text: Convert {h} hours to minutes.
patterns.hint: 1 hour = 60 minutes.
patterns.explanation: {h} × 60 = {60 * h} minutes.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 minutes per hour or confuses clock time with duration.
patterns.notes: 2 to 24 hours.

patterns.text: {ev} lasts {h} {'hour' if h == 1 else 'hours'}. How many {b}-minute sessions fit into it exactly?
patterns.hint: Change the hours to minutes, then divide by {b}.
patterns.explanation: {h} × 60 = {60 * h} minutes. {60 * h} ÷ {b} = {60 * h // b} sessions.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 minutes per hour or confuses clock time with duration.
patterns.notes: 1 to 8 hours; sessions of 10, 15, 20 or 30 minutes, always exact.

patterns.text: {ev} lasts {60 * h} minutes. How many hours is that?
patterns.hint: Every 60 minutes make 1 hour.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 minutes per hour or confuses clock time with duration.
patterns.notes: 2 to 12 whole hours.

patterns.text: Which is longer: {a} hours or {60 * a + d} minutes?

options.correct: 'The hours' if d < 0 else ('The minutes' if d > 0 else 'They are the same length')

wrong.mistake: compares the numbers without changing to the same unit

wrong.expr: 'They are the same length' if d != 0 else 'The minutes'
wrong.mistake: changes hours to minutes using 100 minutes in an hour, or guesses
thinks hours and minutes cannot be compared

patterns.hint: Change the hours to minutes first: 1 hour = 60 minutes.
patterns.explanation: {a} hours = {60 * a} minutes, and the other time is {60 * a + d} minutes, so {'the hours are longer' if d < 0 else ('the minutes are longer' if d > 0 else 'they are the same length')}.
patterns.misconception: Uses 100 minutes per hour or confuses clock time with duration.
patterns.notes: 2 to 6 hours against a number of minutes 40 less to 40 more than that; the answer changes with the copy.

patterns.text: Convert {h} {'hour' if h == 1 else 'hours'} {m} minutes to minutes.
patterns.hint: Change the hours to minutes, then add the extra minutes.
patterns.misconception: Writes the remainder as a decimal part of an hour without conversion.
patterns.notes: 1 to 5 hours and 5 to 55 minutes.

patterns.text: Write {t} minutes in hours and minutes. Enter hours; minutes.
patterns.hint: Take out as many 60s as you can. What is left is the minutes.
patterns.misconception: Writes the remainder as a decimal part of an hour without conversion.
patterns.notes: 65 to 355 minutes, never whole hours; two boxes.

patterns.text: How many minutes longer is {a} hours than {b} {'hour' if b == 1 else 'hours'} {c} minutes?
patterns.hint: Change both to minutes, then subtract.
patterns.explanation: {a} h = {60 * a} min; {b} h {c} min = {60 * b + c} min. {60 * a} − {60 * b + c} = {60 * a - 60 * b - c} minutes.
patterns.misconception: Writes the remainder as a decimal part of an hour without conversion.
patterns.notes: 2 to 6 whole hours against a shorter time with 5 to 55 minutes.

patterns.text: Add {d} minutes to a time of {h} {'hour' if h == 1 else 'hours'} {m} minutes. Write the answer in hours and minutes. Enter hours; minutes.

steps.text: Adds the minutes: {m} + {d} = {m + d} minutes.
Regroups 60 minutes as 1 hour: {h + (m + d) // 60} hr {(m + d) % 60} min.

patterns.hint: Add the minutes. If you get 60 or more, make an hour.
patterns.explanation: {m} + {d} = {m + d} minutes = 1 hr {(m + d) % 60} min. Total: {h + 1} hr {(m + d) % 60} min.
patterns.misconception: Writes the remainder as a decimal part of an hour without conversion.
patterns.notes: The minutes always add to 60 or more, so the child must regroup; two boxes.

patterns.text: Convert {m} {'minute' if m == 1 else 'minutes'} {s} seconds to seconds.
patterns.hint: Change the minutes to seconds, then add the extra seconds.
patterns.misconception: Leaves 60 or more seconds in the seconds part of a mixed duration.
patterns.notes: 1 to 9 minutes and 5 to 55 seconds.

patterns.text: {dev} shows {t} seconds. How many complete minutes is that?
patterns.hint: How many 60s fit into {t}?
patterns.explanation: {t} = {t // 60} × 60 + {t % 60}, so {t // 60} complete minutes.
patterns.misconception: Leaves 60 or more seconds in the seconds part of a mixed duration.
patterns.notes: 70 to 590 seconds, never a whole number of minutes.

patterns.text: How many seconds shorter is {a} {'minute' if a == 1 else 'minutes'} {b} seconds than {c} minutes?
patterns.hint: Change both times to seconds, then subtract.
patterns.explanation: {c} min = {60 * c} sec; {a} min {b} sec = {60 * a + b} sec. {60 * c} − {60 * a + b} = {60 * c - 60 * a - b} seconds.
patterns.misconception: Leaves 60 or more seconds in the seconds part of a mixed duration.
patterns.notes: A time of 1 to 8 minutes and 5 to 55 seconds against 3 to 9 whole minutes.

patterns.text: Add {s} seconds to {m} {'minute' if m == 1 else 'minutes'} {r} seconds. Write the answer in minutes and seconds. Enter minutes; seconds.

steps.text: Adds the seconds: {r} + {s} = {r + s} seconds.
Regroups 60 seconds as 1 minute: {m + 1} min {r + s - 60} sec.

patterns.hint: Add the seconds. If you get 60 or more, make a minute.
patterns.explanation: {r} + {s} = {r + s} seconds = 1 min {r + s - 60} sec. Total: {m + 1} min {r + s - 60} sec.
patterns.misconception: Leaves 60 or more seconds in the seconds part of a mixed duration.
patterns.notes: The seconds always add to 60 or more, so the child must regroup; two boxes.

patterns.responseFormat: Clock time in two boxes (hours; minutes)
patterns.text: Write {t.h}:{'0' if (m) < 10 else ''}{m} {t.ap} in 24-hour time. Enter hours; minutes.
patterns.hint: Morning times keep their hour (but 12 a.m. is 00). Afternoon and evening times add 12 (but 12 p.m. stays 12).
patterns.explanation: {t.h}:{'0' if (m) < 10 else ''}{m} {t.ap} is {'0' if (t.H) < 10 else ''}{t.H}:{'0' if (m) < 10 else ''}{m} in 24-hour time.
patterns.misconception: Adds 12 to morning times, writes p.m. with 24-hour time, or confuses 12 noon with 12 midnight.
patterns.notes: Every hour 1 to 12, a.m. and p.m., including 12 a.m. (00) and 12 p.m. (12); minutes 05 to 55; two boxes.

patterns.text: A train leaves at {'0' if t.H < 10 else ''}{t.H}:{'0' if t.m < 10 else ''}{t.m} (24-hour time). What is this in 12-hour time?

wrong.mistake: subtracts 12 but writes a.m. for an afternoon or evening time
subtracts 10 instead of 12
counts on from 13:00 as 2 o'clock, getting one hour too many

patterns.hint: For 13:00 and later, subtract 12 from the hour and write p.m.
patterns.explanation: {t.H} − 12 = {t.H - 12}, so it is {t.c}.
patterns.misconception: Adds 12 to morning times, writes p.m. with 24-hour time, or confuses 12 noon with 12 midnight.
patterns.notes: Times from 13:00 to 22:55 (so every wrong choice is still a real 12-hour time).

patterns.text: {ev} runs from {h1}:{'0' if (m1) < 10 else ''}{m1} a.m. to {h2}:{'0' if (m2) < 10 else ''}{m2} p.m. on the same day. How long does it last? Enter hours; minutes.

steps.text: Changes to 24-hour time: {'0' if (h1) < 10 else ''}{h1}:{'0' if (m1) < 10 else ''}{m1} to {'0' if (h2 + 12) < 10 else ''}{h2 + 12}:{'0' if (m2) < 10 else ''}{m2} (or counts to 12 noon and on).

patterns.hint: Change {h2}:{'0' if (m2) < 10 else ''}{m2} p.m. to 24-hour time first, or count up to 12 noon and then on.
patterns.misconception: Adds 12 to morning times, writes p.m. with 24-hour time, or confuses 12 noon with 12 midnight.
patterns.notes: A morning start (7 to 11 a.m.) and an afternoon end (1 to 5 p.m.) on the same day; crosses 12 noon; two boxes.

patterns.text: {pl} opens at {a} a.m. and closes at {cl}:00 (24-hour time). For how many hours is it open?
patterns.hint: In 24-hour time, {a} a.m. keeps its hour: {a}. Then subtract.
patterns.explanation: {a} a.m. is {'0' if a < 10 else ''}{a}:00. From {'0' if a < 10 else ''}{a}:00 to {cl}:00 is {cl} − {a} = {cl - a} hours.
patterns.misconception: Adds 12 to morning times, writes p.m. with 24-hour time, or confuses 12 noon with 12 midnight.
patterns.notes: Opening 6 to 11 a.m., closing 17:00 to 22:00, whole hours.

patterns.text: An activity starts at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} and ends at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a + d) < 10 else ''}{a + d}. How many minutes does it last?
patterns.hint: Both times are in the same hour, so subtract the minutes.
patterns.explanation: {a + d} − {a} = {d} minutes.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts clock digits as whole numbers or includes the starting minute as an extra minute.
patterns.notes: Times within one hour, 6 to 19 minutes apart.

patterns.text: From {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a}, how many minutes are there until the next full hour?
patterns.hint: The next full hour is {'0' if (h + 1) < 10 else ''}{h + 1}:{'0' if (0) < 10 else ''}{0}. How many minutes from {a} to 60?
patterns.explanation: 60 − {a} = {60 - a} minutes, so the next full hour, {'0' if (h + 1) < 10 else ''}{h + 1}:{'0' if (0) < 10 else ''}{0}, is {60 - a} minutes away.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts clock digits as whole numbers or includes the starting minute as an extra minute.
patterns.notes: Any minute 03 to 57 past 07 to 18.

patterns.responseFormat: Clock time in two boxes (hours; minutes)
patterns.text: {ev} ends at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (e) < 10 else ''}{e} after {d} minutes. At what time did it begin? Show your working. Enter hours; minutes.

steps.text: Counts back {d} minutes from {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (e) < 10 else ''}{e} (subtracts {d} from {e}).
Gives the start time {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (e - d) < 10 else ''}{e - d}.

patterns.hint: Count back {d} minutes from the end.
patterns.explanation: {e} − {d} = {e - d}, so it began at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (e - d) < 10 else ''}{e - d}.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts clock digits as whole numbers or includes the starting minute as an extra minute.
patterns.notes: Start and end in the same hour; two boxes.

patterns.text: Which calculation gives the number of minutes from {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (t.a) < 10 else ''}{t.a} to {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (t.b) < 10 else ''}{t.b}?

wrong.mistake: adds the two minute readings
counts both the starting and the ending minute
counts to the end of the hour when the times are in the same hour

patterns.hint: Both times are in the same hour. Take the earlier minutes from the later ones.
patterns.explanation: {t.b} − {t.a} = {t.b - t.a} minutes.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts clock digits as whole numbers or includes the starting minute as an extra minute.
patterns.notes: Times in the same hour, 11 to 19 minutes apart.

patterns.text: Find the time in minutes from {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} to {'0' if (h + k) < 10 else ''}{h + k}:{'0' if (b) < 10 else ''}{b}.
patterns.hint: Count to the next full hour, then on to the end.
patterns.explanation: From {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} to {'0' if (h + 1) < 10 else ''}{h + 1}:{'0' if (0) < 10 else ''}{0} is {60 - a} minutes; then {60 * (k - 1) + b} more. Total {60 * k + b - a} minutes.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts minutes without regrouping or treats one hour as 100 minutes.
patterns.notes: Across one or two hours.

patterns.text: A bus journey from {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} to {'0' if (h + 1) < 10 else ''}{h + 1}:{'0' if (b) < 10 else ''}{b} includes a {st}-minute stop. How many minutes was the bus moving?
patterns.hint: Find the whole time first, then take away the stop.
patterns.explanation: Whole journey: {60 + b - a} minutes. Moving: {60 + b - a} − {st} = {60 + b - a - st} minutes.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts minutes without regrouping or treats one hour as 100 minutes.
patterns.notes: A journey across one hour with a 5 to 20 minute stop.

patterns.text: A practice session runs from {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} to {'0' if (h + k) < 10 else ''}{h + k}:{'0' if (b) < 10 else ''}{b}. How long is it in hours and minutes? Enter hours; minutes.

steps.text: Sees that {b} is less than {a}, so borrows 1 hour as 60 minutes.
Gets {k - 1} h {60 + b - a} min.

patterns.hint: The end minutes are fewer than the start minutes, so borrow an hour.
patterns.explanation: {'0' if (h + k) < 10 else ''}{h + k}:{'0' if (b) < 10 else ''}{b} − {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a}: borrow 1 hour, {60 + b} − {a} = {60 + b - a} minutes and {k - 1} {'hour' if (k - 1) == 1 else 'hours'}. So {k - 1} h {60 + b - a} min.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts minutes without regrouping or treats one hour as 100 minutes.
patterns.notes: The end minutes are always smaller than the start minutes, so the child must regroup; 1 to 2 hours and some minutes, never under an hour; two boxes.

patterns.text: A bus should take {d} minutes for a trip. One day it leaves at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} and arrives at {'0' if (h + (a + d + late) // 60) < 10 else ''}{h + (a + d + late) // 60}:{'0' if ((a + d + late) % 60) < 10 else ''}{(a + d + late) % 60}. How many minutes late is it?
patterns.hint: Find how long the trip really took, then compare with {d} minutes.
patterns.explanation: The trip took {d + late} minutes, which is {d + late} − {d} = {late} minutes more than it should.
patterns.misconception: Subtracts minutes without regrouping or treats one hour as 100 minutes.
patterns.notes: A trip of 40 to 75 minutes arriving 5 to 25 minutes late; the times cross the hour.

patterns.responseFormat: Clock time in two boxes (hours; minutes)
patterns.text: A lesson starts at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} and lasts {d} minutes. At what time does it finish? Enter hours; minutes.
patterns.hint: Add the minutes. If you reach 60, move on to the next hour.
patterns.explanation: {a} + {d} = {a + d} minutes after {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (0) < 10 else ''}{0}, so it finishes at {'0' if (h + (a + d) // 60) < 10 else ''}{h + (a + d) // 60}:{'0' if ((a + d) % 60) < 10 else ''}{(a + d) % 60}.
patterns.misconception: Adds minutes without carrying each complete group of 60 into hours.
patterns.notes: Starts 07:05 to 15:55, lessons of 25 to 50 minutes; often crosses the hour; two boxes.

patterns.responseFormat: Clock time in two boxes (hours; minutes)
patterns.text: {ev} leaves at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a} and the journey takes {x} {'hour' if x == 1 else 'hours'} {y} minutes. At what time does it arrive? Enter hours; minutes.
patterns.hint: Add the hours, then the minutes. If the minutes reach 60, add another hour.
patterns.misconception: Adds minutes without carrying each complete group of 60 into hours.
patterns.notes: Journeys of 1 to 3 hours and 10 to 50 minutes, arriving the same day; two boxes.

patterns.text: A class starts at {t.st} and lasts {t.d} minutes. When does it finish?

wrong.mistake: takes 60 from the minutes but forgets to carry the hour
adds a whole hour instead of the minutes
counts back instead of on

patterns.hint: Add the minutes. 60 minutes make the next hour.
patterns.explanation: {t.a} + {t.d} = {t.a + t.d} minutes = 1 hour {t.a + t.d - 60} minutes, so it finishes at {t.c}.
patterns.misconception: Adds minutes without carrying each complete group of 60 into hours.
patterns.notes: Starts at 20 to 55 minutes past the hour with 30 to 55 minutes added, so the minutes always pass 60; every choice is a real clock time.

patterns.responseFormat: Clock time in two boxes (hours; minutes)
patterns.text: {ev} was planned to finish at {'0' if (h) < 10 else ''}{h}:{'0' if (a) < 10 else ''}{a}. It runs {e} minutes over time. At what time does it finish now? Show your working. Enter hours; minutes.

steps.text: Adds the minutes: {a} + {e} = {a + e}.
